newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, February 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, February 18.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Local elections for 1,138 Italian cities and towns, including Milan and Turin, will take place on April 27 (all).

* After meeting with German businessmen and bankers in Munich and Frankfurt, prime minister Romano Prodi said Italy would not ask for a weakening of the criteria for joining EMU and that there was no need to delay Italy's entry (all).

* In an interview Martin Kohlhaussen, chairman of German bank Commerzbank, says "if a country has been only lately successful in its fight against public debt and inflation, it should delay its entry into EMU" (Corriere della Sera).
* Leftist PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema said that a mini-budget later this year was inevitable but added: "I don't think it will be a budget of a devastating size" (all).
* Prodi said Italian inflation could fall further in the near term but much depended also on international factors (all).
* Labour minister Tiziano Treu said the government will eliminate the remaining "golden pensions" granting special privileges to some working categories (all).
* After 8 years of job freeze, car maker Fiat will hire 2000 people, half in the Turin area, with fixed-term contracts (all).
* Paolo Forlin, managing director of publisher Mondadori, which is controlled by former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest group, reportedly resigned after six months (Sole 24 Ore).

* Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio in a letter to Labour minister Treu and Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi reportedly suggested measures to help Italy's banks streamline their bloated payrolls. Fazio is quoted as saying layoffs should concern at least 10 percent of bank personnel, estimated at around 30,000 employees (Sole 24 Ore, La Stampa).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
